heading: Liji 27 · Fang Ji 坊記 · Record Of The Dykes · Fang Ji 35 … Fang Ji 38

items.text: Do not allow your wife to be present at grand public entertainments.
items.quote: the presence of the wife at the grand entertainments was disallowed

items.text: Do not have interviews with the son of a widow.
items.quote: With the son of a widow one does not have interviews

items.text: When driving your wife in a carriage, advance your left hand to avoid touching her.
items.quote: in driving his wife in a carriage, a husband advances his left hand

items.text: When a married relative such as a young aunt, sister, or daughter returns to her father's house, no male relative should sit on the same mat with her.
items.quote: when a young aunt, a sister, or a daughter has been married, and returns (to her father's house), no male can sit on the same mat with her
items.needs_role: male kin; married aunt/sister/daughter returned to her father's house

items.text: A widow must not wail at night.
items.quote: a widow should not wail at night

items.text: When a married woman is ill, do not ask about the nature of her illness.
items.quote: when a wife is ill, in asking for her, the nature of her illness should not be mentioned

items.text: Go in person to meet your bride and bring her to your home.
items.quote: the son-in-law should go in person to meet the bride

items.text: Bring your daughter forward and give her to the son-in-law when he comes to meet her.
items.quote: they bring her forward, and give her to him

heading: Liji 27 · Fang Ji 坊記 · Record Of The Dykes · Fang Ji 1 … Fang Ji 13

items.text: Do not be stubborn or rebellious against those above you; accept their authority.
items.quote: men in positions of honour should not be intractable to those above them

items.text: Keep your family quiet and at peace, even when it is numerous and strong.
items.quote: a family that is numerous (and strong) yet remains quiet and at peace

items.text: Yield to one another; give place according to rank.
items.quote: the people (are taught to) give place to one another

items.text: Acknowledge only one master in your family; do not set up rival authorities.
items.quote: nor two masters in a family

items.text: In bestowing advantages and rewards, put the dead first and the living after; do not act contrary to the character of the dead.
items.quote: advantages and rewards are given to the dead first, and to the living afterwards

items.text: Consider and be guided by the words of those under you, so that they receive your commands as from Heaven.
items.quote: If superiors consider and are guided by the words of the people, the people receive their gifts or commands as if they were from Heaven.

items.text: Receive the gifts and commands of your superior as if they were from Heaven.
items.quote: receive their gifts or commands as if they were from Heaven

items.text: Ascribe what is good to others and what is wrong to yourself, so that contentions and dissatisfactions cease.
items.quote: If (the ruler) ascribe what is good to others, and what is wrong to himself, the people will not contend

items.text: Think much of the persons of your family and little of the emoluments you bestow on them.
items.quote: thinks much of the men and little of the emoluments (which he bestows on them)

items.text: Keep your speech under control; do not be forward to speak.
items.quote: a superior man keeps his speech under control, while the small man is forward to speak

heading: Liji 27 · Fang Ji 坊記 · Record Of The Dykes · Fang Ji 14 … Fang Ji 27

items.text: Ascribe what is good to your father and what is wrong to yourself.
items.quote: If (a ruler, being a son,) ascribe what is good to his father, and what is wrong to himself

items.text: Do not dwell on your parents' faults; revere their virtues.
items.quote: forget and not make much of the errors of his father, and will show his reverence for his excellence

items.text: Obey their commands without complaint; remonstrate gently; do not murmur when they punish you.
items.quote: To obey (his parents') commands without angry (complaint); to remonstrate with them gently without being weary; and not to murmur against them, though they punish him

items.text: Cultivate harmony with all your parents' kindred as an act of filial piety.
items.quote: To cultivate harmony with all the kindred of parents may be pronounced filial

items.text: Do not presume upon the belongings of your father's friends; expand your filial reverence.
items.quote: (A son) may ride in the chariot of an intimate friend of his father, but he should not wear his robes.

items.text: Support your parents, but also reverence them; support alone is not enough.
items.quote: Small men are all able to support their parents. If the superior man do not also reverence them

items.text: Do not hold the same official position as your father, so that the honor due him is not diminished.
items.quote: Father and son should not, be in the same (official) position;--to magnify the reverence (due to the father).

items.text: In your parents' presence, do not call yourself old, do not speak of kindness due from them, and do not sigh.
items.quote: Before his parents (a son) should not speak of himself as old

items.text: Repair the ancestral temple and reverently perform sacrifices for the dead.
items.quote: The repairing of the ancestral temple and the reverential performance of the sacrifices were intended to teach the people to follow their dead with their filial duty.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment (Exodus 20:3) and Deuteronomy 6:14.

items.text: Observe days of fasting and vigil, and reverence the personator of the dead.
items.quote: seven days of fasting, and the three days of vigil and adjustment of the thoughts; appointment of the one man to act as the personator of the dead
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment (Exodus 20:3) and Deuteronomy 6:14.

items.text: Assemble all your kindred for the sacrificial meal to cultivate harmony.
items.quote: The ruler takes the opportunity of the spirits and flesh of his sacrifice to assemble all the members of his kindred

heading: Liji 27 · Fang Ji 坊記 · Record Of The Dykes · Fang Ji 28 … Fang Ji 34

items.text: Perform the funeral and burial rites for your departed kinsmen, as the last duties you owe them.
items.quote: (These services in connexion with) death are the last duties which the people have to pay (to their departed).

items.text: Continue to show filial piety to your departed parents by mourning and receiving condolences as if they were still present.
items.quote: are designed to teach the filial to continue their filial duty even to the dead.

items.text: While mourning for your father is unfinished, do not take his title or authority; show that you do not contend with him.
items.quote: Until the mourning rites are finished, a son is not styled 'Ruler:'--showing the people that there ought to be no contention (between father and son).

items.text: Submit to your elder brother as you would to an elder, serving him without double-mindedness.
items.quote: brotherly submission to the service of elders

items.text: Mourn your father for three years, as you would mourn your ruler, without doubting the duty you owe.
items.quote: The mourning for a father lasts for three years, and that for a ruler the same time

items.text: While your parents are alive, do not treat your wealth as your own or use it for your private purposes; hold it as theirs.
items.quote: While his parents are alive, a son should not dare to consider his wealth as his own, nor to hold any of it as for his own private use

items.text: While your parents are alive, do not accept gifts of a carriage and team, lest you take honor that belongs to them.
items.quote: While his parents are alive, the gifts presented to a son should not extend to a carriage and its team

items.text: Leave gleanings in your field for the widow, and do not take every profit you might.
items.quote: There shall be handfuls left on the ground, And ears here and there left untouched; For the benefit of the widow.
